extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and Korean Intellectual Property Office examiners
extracted.subtask_short: Korean patent claim drafting and unity rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to draft claims (format, independent vs dependent, numbering, composition claims, deferral of claims) and how examiners determine unity of invention under the Korean Patent Act and its Enforcement Decree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alloy composition claims must sum to 100%
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim directed to alloy should set forth the invention so that composition range of each component in alloy should be added up to be 100%. Regardless of whether the claim is stated as a close claim (“consisting of”) or an open claim (“comprising”), the total sum of composition range should not be over or under 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one component is given as a relative ratio based on another component the composition ratio is deemed clear. Do not specify only main component while omitting additive components — structure/phase/application/property may vary with additives. Example: a copper alloy claim whose minimum of Cu plus maximums of others sums to less than 100% is unclear and not accepted. Also, list components and recite composition ranges exactly (see Part IX Ch.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims shall recite matters necessary to specify the invention (Article 42(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must recite such matters regarded necessary to specify what is sought for patent protection as structures, methods, functions and materials or combination thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, an invention may be defined by effect or operation method rather than physical structure; if an invention can be clearly specified this is permitted at applicant's choice. The provision itself is not a basis for rejection/invalidity — examiners must not reject or invalidate based solely on this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-claims system: claims determine protection scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The law prescribes how claims included in a specification must be drafted so they serve to determine the scope of protection of the claimed invention; the Korean Patent Act adopts a system of multiple claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 5 of the Enforcement Decree prescribes requirements for claim drafting under the multiple-claims system. Claims should be drafted to clearly define protection and follow statutory form and numbering rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim concept: narrowing or adding limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent claims are those that narrow or add further limitations to specify an independent claim (specifying by adding technical elements or narrowing a generic concept to a species).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim narrows or adds to another claim in content but does not formally refer to it, it is not a dependent claim. Conversely, a claim that formally refers to an independent claim but does not narrow/add limitations (e.g., substituting A with B) is likewise not a dependent claim. Note Article 5(1) allows claims that substantiate independent claims by narrowing/adding to be presented as dependent, but they may also be presented as independent — it's not mandatory to use dependent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent-claim presentation and permitted references (Article 5(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent claims shall be presented without referring to other claims in the form of standing alone. However, independent claims can refer to other claims within the scope in which the invention can be clearly understood to avoid redundant description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted examples: 'A product of ... manufactured by the method of claim 0', 'A method of manufacturing a product of claim 0 by ...', etc. Claims that decrease elements or substitute subject matter of referred claims are treated as independent (not dependent). The provision is non-binding for rejection — examiners should not rely solely on it to reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper number of claims according to nature of the invention (Article 5(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be presented in a proper number according to the nature of the invention; this is distinct from unity issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper cases include: (i) two or more inventions of different categories recited in one claim (e.g., chemical compound and a contact lens using it), (ii) two or more subject matters included in one claim, (iii) redundant identical claims (identical wording or merely different expressions with identical meaning), (iv) multiple claims technically referred to many times within a single claim (referring to many claims inside one claim) which may cause confusion. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for referring to other claims: include claim numbers (Article 5(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim referring to other claims shall contain the number(s) of the claims referred to and be entered in an accepted manner (e.g., 'A method of ... in claim 0', 'A device of ... in any from claim 0 to claim 0').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised Article 5(4) (promulgated June 28, 2013) applies to all claims making reference to other claims for applications examined after July 1, 2013. Use consistent numbering and phrasing when referring to other claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative numbering when referring to multiple claims (Article 5(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim refers to two or more claims, the claims referred to shall be numbered alternatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed phrasings and their semantics are illustrated: 'in claim 1 or claim 2', 'in any of claims 1 to 3', 'in claim 1, claim 2 or claim 3', 'in any of claims 1 to 7 and claims 9-11', etc. The guide explains how 'any of' and conjunctions ('and'/'or') affect limitation and alternative listing recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: No referencing chains among claims that refer to multiple claims (Article 5(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims referring to two or more claims cannot refer to other claims that themselves refer to two or more claims (to prevent interpretative difficulties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show prohibited chains where Claim 4 refers to Claim 2 or Claim 3 and Claim 3 already refers to Claim 1 or Claim 2. The provision does not apply to claims depending on only one claim. Examiners shall notify a ground for rejection citing violation of Article 42(8) when such prohibited referencing occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim referred-to must precede referring claim (Article 5(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim referred to by another claim should precede the other claim in numbering to facilitate interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim refers to itself or refers to a later-numbered claim, an examiner shall notify a ground for rejection citing violation of Article 42(8) and Article 5(7) or cite indefiniteness under Article 42(4)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation: each claim on a new line and sequential numbering (Article 5(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim shall be presented in a new line and the claims shall be numbered in sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To clearly define configuration even within a single claim, a claim can be presented in several lines — e.g., multi-step method claims listing steps (A),(B),(C),(D) are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of submission of claims (system and deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may file a specification without including claims (deferral system) but must submit claims by set deadlines (the time limit for submission of claims), otherwise the application is deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: allow speedy filing and time to prepare claims. Claims must be submitted by three months after notification of intention of a request for examination or by 1 year 2 months (1 year 6 months for apps filed before Dec 31, 2014) from the priority date. If not submitted by deadlines the application is deemed withdrawn the day after deadline. If an application without claims requests examination, examiner should give opportunity for explanation and return it. Such applications are not laid open for publication. Special rules allow claim submission windows for divisional/converted applications filed after Jan 1, 2015 (claims until 30 days from filing). Whether deferral applied is determined by presence/absence of 'Patent Claims' identification symbols in Annexed Form no.15 — if present, deferral is not deemed employed even if claim text blank or contains only punctuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention: general test (Article 45 and Art.6 Enforcement Decree)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application shall be filed for each invention, but may be filed for a group of inventions linked so as to form a single general inventive concept. Requirements: (1) claimed inventions shall be technologically correlated; (2) claimed inventions shall have the same or corresponding technological features — these technological features are the improved features over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'special technical features' concept is used to determine unity; these need not be identical but must be same or corresponding (e.g., different means to provide same function). They must involve novelty and inventive step over relevant prior art. Unity is determined considering the invention as a whole and by comparing to prior art; in some cases unity can be assessed a priori, in others after prior art search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for determining unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity is determined by selecting a first invention, specifying its special technical features (improvements over prior art), selecting a second invention and its special technical features, and checking whether those features are the same or corresponding; if so, they form a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first invention (main invention) is chosen independent of claim order. Repeat the process for other claims; the first technical group and inventions forming it are selected as subject to examination. Examination of patentability (novelty, inventive step, etc.) for the invention subject to examination proceeds. If lack of unity is notified, examiner must specify that the concerned inventions do not share the same or corresponding special technical features characterizing the first technical group. Lack of unity is a ground for rejection (to allow amendment/divisional filing) but not a ground for invalidation; examiners need not require amendment where examination can be completed without additional search (e.g., where all claims are unpatentable based on searched prior art).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and edge cases for unity determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Various examples illustrate when unity is or is not met: dependent claims that include independent claim's special technical features satisfy unity; generic/species, combination/sub-combination, corresponding features (e.g., timebase expander vs compressor) can meet unity; claims reciting unrelated special technical features do not have unity between them; claims where features are not single (A, B, and A+B) meet unity between A and A+B and between B and A+B but not between A and B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples to identify common features or corresponding features. When common features are later shown not to be improvements over prior art, unity may be lost a posteriori. Examiner should consider these examples when applying the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity between product and its manufacturing method depends on 'suitability'
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity between a product invention and the manufacturing method of that product is determined based on whether the manufacturing method is 'suitable' for manufacture of the product (i.e., practicing the method manufactures the product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Suitable' does not require exclusivity — product may be manufacturable by other methods and the method may be used for other products. Examples: chemical X and method to manufacture chemical X share the common special technical feature chemical X; corrugated cardboard and method steps producing that cardboard are 'suitable' and thus unity is met.
